calendar.name: Big Bear — Local Events
calendar.description: A practical, independently curated calendar of worthwhile Big Bear Valley events, with lineups, prices, logistics, source links, conflicts, and honest TBD flags.

price_policy: Free events are the default target
$20–40: include when the experience is genuinely worthwhile or distinctive
$40–50: include selectively for exceptional concerts, motorsports, wildlife or similarly strong experiences
Over $50: normally exclude unless exceptional enough to justify a rare exception
Unknown price: include as details_tbd when the event is relevant and likely free or inexpensive, so the calendar can serve as a reminder to investigate
priorities: Karaoke, trivia, line dancing, Wyatt’s nights and other useful recurring local nightlife
Country, punk, metal and distinctive local live music
Astronomy, wildlife, plants, geology and science
Environmental volunteering and hands-on community groups
Weird, unusual and unmistakably mountain-town events
boundaries: Keep transportation and service schedules outside the events calendar
Use official organizer sources first and preserve meaningful source conflicts in TBD notes
Do not omit a promising event solely because its exact price or start time is unpublished; use a clearly labeled TBD reminder when its date and identity are credible
Recurring listings still need a supported cadence or dated occurrence; never invent dates from an old or ambiguous schedule
Do not re-add a permanently excluded event under a new ID

permanent_exclusions.reason: The $40–$75 package duplicates Scenic Sky Chair access already included with the user’s pass, advertises no vegetarian buffet option, and provides no named performer or date-specific distinction.

retired.reason: Dropped as a curation call, not a cancellation — the event still runs. The buffet is tri-tip and grilled salmon with no advertised vegetarian option, the official page states pass-holder discounts are not applicable, and all twelve dates are described identically with no named performer, so nothing distinguishes one date from another. At $40–$75 for a lift ride that an Ikon pass already covers, it does not earn its place on a locals calendar.
